newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean banks cut prime rates by 0.25 pct points.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean banks cut prime rates by 0.25 pct points.

text.p: South Korean commercial banks said on Friday they were cutting their prime rates by 0.25 percentage points in line with a cut in reserve requirements for banks.
The Bank of Korea, the central bank, said last month it lowered the reserve requirement ratio to an average of 5.5 percent, effective from today, from 7.4 percent.
Cho Hung Bank, Korea First Bank, Hanil Bank and six other commercial banks cut their prime lending rates to 8.5 percent from 8.75 percent.
"We lowered out prime rates by 0.25 percentage points in compliance with the central bank's reserve ratio cut," said Park Young-suk, a spokesman at Cho Hung Bank.
SEOULBANK, Hana Bank and five other commercial banks lowered or would soon lower their prime rates to 8.75 percent from 9.0 percent, officials of the banks said.
Two smaller banks cut their prime rates by 0.25 percentage points to 9.0 percent.

Banking analysts said the 0.25 percentage point cut in the prime rates would probably be the maximum commercial banks could afford without eroding profitability, following the reserve ratio adjustment.
The reserve requirement is the portion of money banks have to set aside with the central bank out of total deposits that they receive.
